figurative_meaning_en: The confluence or meeting point of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers
example_sentences_in_bangla: কুম্ভমেলায় লক্ষ লক্ষ ভক্ত ত্রিবেণীতে স্নান করেন।
প্রয়াগের ত্রিবেণীসংগম হিন্দুধর্মের একটি পবিত্র স্থান।
example_sentences_in_english: Millions of devotees bathe at Triveni during the Kumbh Mela.
The Triveni Sangam in Prayag is a sacred site in Hinduism.
history: Triveni Sangam is located at Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) in Uttar Pradesh, India, and is the venue for the Kumbh Mela, one of the largest religious gatherings in the world.
It is mythologically significant as the point where the invisible Saraswati River joins the Ganga and Yamuna, symbolizing the union of knowledge, purity, and devotion.
note: This idiom primarily refers to the specific sacred geographical location rather than a general figurative expression, though it evokes themes of convergence and spirituality in Bengali cultural discourse.
